newsitem.title: UK: UK services sector grows at slightly slower rate.
newsitem.headline: UK services sector grows at slightly slower rate.

text.p: Britain's services sector grew strongly in July but the PMI business activity index dipped for the second month in succession, signalling a slight moderation in the pace of growth, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
Its monthly Report on Services, sponsored by Reuters, showed the first signs that the strong pound is hurting services firms as well as manufacturers.
"Activity at panel member companies rose to meet a further sharp rise in the amount of new business placed during the month," the CIPS said.

"Buoyant consumer confidence was again reported to have played a key role in boosting demand, but the July survey saw the first evidence of the strength of the pound damaging the competitiveness of UK service providers, resulting in a slight slowing in the rate of growth of new business."
The seasonally adjusted business activity index dipped to 62.1 from 62.9 in June. Any reading above 50 signals an expansion.
The average prices charged index was 52.1 compared with 53.4 in June, showing the ninth consecutive rise in prices, but the rate of growth was the slowest since last December.

"The growth of labour costs, combined with higher interest rates and higher fuel costs (resulting from the budget), led to a further increase in average input prices and the first acceleration in the rate of input price inflation since April."
"Rising input prices again encouraged firms to pass higher costs onto customers. Rates charges by service providers have now risen for nine successive months.

"However, as seen throughout this period, strong competitive pressures limited the scope for companies to pass on higher costs. Thus, whereas one in five companies saw their average input prices rise in July only one in ten were able to raise their charges."
The amount of business outstanding increased.
"In order to clear backlogs, and meet the current strength of demand, employment was again increased. One in five companies took on new permanent staff in July," the CIPS said.
Companies reported continued skill shortages which often resulted in higher salaries.
The strong pound forced increasing numbers of firms to cut charges, leading to the weakest growth in rates charged seen since last December.

Firms generally remained optimistic about future growth in activity, with two-thirds of the survey panel expecting an increase over the next year. "However, the strength of the pound and fears of higher interest rates caused the Expectations Index to drop to the lowest level recorded over the thirteen month history of this survey," the CIPS said.
Following are indices from the services survey (seasonally adjusted except for business expectations, which is unadjusted):
July June
Business activity 62.1 62.9
Incoming new business 59.2 60.8
Outstanding business 54.3 55.8
Employment 55.7 55.2
Average prices charged 52.1 53.4
Average input prices 57.7 57.4
Business expectations 79.8 83.9
NOTE: The survey covers transport and communication, financial intermediation, business services, personal services, hotels and restaurants.

The results are given by questions asked, showing the percentage of respondents reporting an improvement, deterioration, or no change on the previous month. From these percentages an index is derived, with a level of 50.0 signalling no change on the previous month, above 50 signals an increase or improvement, below 50 a decrease or deterioration.
-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
